messages:
maya: CI microbench failed on PR-17699, threshold diff +9% on kv-cache-hitrate for short-stream test. saw this in pipeline 5/8.
ci-bench-bot: [FAIL] pr/17699 microbench/short-stream: kv_hit_rate down 9.2% (threshold 5%). logs: https://ci.internal/reports/17699
owen: ugh. I ran the same bench locally, reproduced roughly +7% drop. only when run under the CI sampling harness, not in long-run harness.
liam: any recent changes touching batch timer or prefetch window in that PR?
maya: PR touches batcher timer: reduced max_wait_ms from 8 -> 4 to lower avg latency. also a separate commit in the same PR tweaked kernel warmup gating (less aggressive warmup).
jenny: timeline makes me suspicious of the timer change aligning with prefetch/kv prefetch window. we saw weird alignment oscillations previously.
tara: can you paste the bench command you used to reproduce?
owen: here's what I ran:
```
./tools/bench --profile --scenario=short-stream --ci-mode --seed=9012
```
liam: I ran a bisect across the merge window. delta jumps exactly at merge commit 7a3f2c7 which includes both the timer change and the kernel gating tweak.
maya: split-bisect would be ideal but both changes shipped in one PR during last merge window.
ci-bench-bot: note: flaky runs flagged by CI. retrying with different sampler.
owen: attaching flamegraph snippet from profile: https://perf.internal/flame/17699/shortstream.svg -> shows hot idle spinning in batcher timer wake path and increased coldkernel invocations.
jenny: that matches a hypothesis: shorter timer causes more frequent tiny batches that miss kv cache warm prefixes -> more coldpath kernel selection and kv misses.
tara: quick experiment idea: push a patch that bumps max_wait_ms back to 6 (not full 8) and rerun CI. if hit rate recovers, we know timer alignment is root.
liam: alternative is to revert kernel warmup gating change (makes warmup less likely) so even small batches still trigger warm path. which is less risky?
owen: revert kernel gating is fiddly and touches selector heuristics. changing timer is a small opt tweak with immediate perf effect.
maya: agree. propose hotfix: set max_wait_ms=6 and add an integration test that exercises short-stream with prefetch on.
ci-bench-bot: [PATCH] /pr/17699-hotfix set batcher.max_wait_ms=6 submitted by maya (run id 5865432120)
ci-bench-bot: [RUN] pr/17699-hotfix microbench/short-stream starting...
ci-bench-bot: [PASS] pr/17699-hotfix microbench/short-stream: kv_hit_rate diff -0.6% (within threshold)
owen: nice. kv hit rate back to baseline under hotfix.
liam: we should still bisect kernel gating independently once we have a proper split PR. create a follow-up that isolates the kernel warmup change.
jenny: agree. also add a CI golden for short-stream seeded runs to catch timer-alignment regressions (reduce sampling noise).
tara: I'll open two follow-ups: 1) revert-ish PR that reintroduces kernel gating change as separate PR for targeted testing, 2) add golden microbench with more seeds.
maya: thanks. I'll merge hotfix to canary to stop rollout blocker and then we can do the proper bisect/testing cycle.
owen: FYI, I left comments on perf dashboard with traces and included the command to repro locally.
liam: good. after canary, let's run a 24h shadow-run to be safe.
maya: noted. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
ci-bench-bot: [MERGE] pr/17699-hotfix merged to canary at 5865432168
